input.hypothesis: The US extends semiconductor export controls to legacy nodes

nodes.statement: The United States extends semiconductor export controls to selected legacy-node equipment
nodes.resolution: Commerce publishes a rule adding defined legacy-node equipment to licensing controls
nodes.rationale: Policy pressure has shifted from frontier AI chips toward the equipment stack that supports military and industrial demand.
assumptions: The rule covers meaningful tool categories rather than a symbolic list

nodes.statement: China responds with procurement guidance favoring domestic semiconductor suppliers
nodes.resolution: A central or provincial procurement notice specifies domestic-sourcing preferences
nodes.rationale: Procurement restrictions are easier to implement than an immediate broad export ban.
assumptions: Domestic suppliers can meet minimum qualification thresholds

nodes.statement: Affected Chinese fabs pull forward equipment and spare-parts orders
nodes.resolution: Supplier commentary reports order acceleration from affected Chinese customers
nodes.rationale: Customers often build buffer inventory ahead of licensing uncertainty.
assumptions: Suppliers can ship before the effective date
nodes.marketQuery: China semiconductor equipment inventory pull forward

nodes.statement: Affected foundries defer part of 2027 capacity expansion
nodes.resolution: Capex guidance is cut by at least 5 percent versus the prior plan
nodes.rationale: Restricted tools and uncertain end demand can delay marginal fab projects.
assumptions: Financing and local subsidies do not fully offset the restriction

nodes.statement: Allied fabs receive a narrow licensing exemption for existing facilities
nodes.resolution: A Commerce clarification grants case-by-case licenses for named allied facilities
nodes.rationale: An exemption can protect allied supply chains without removing leverage over Chinese expansion.
nodes.marketQuery: semiconductor export control allied licensing exemption

nodes.statement: Equipment vendors reduce China revenue guidance
nodes.resolution: A major equipment vendor cuts China revenue guidance by more than 5 percent
nodes.rationale: Licensing uncertainty hits service and spare-parts revenue before new tool orders are formally canceled.
assumptions: China remains a material share of revenue
nodes.marketQuery: semiconductor equipment vendor China revenue guidance cut

nodes.name: VanEck Semiconductor ETF
nodes.rationale: The ETF captures equipment, logic, and memory exposure while diversifying company-specific effects.
assumptions: AI demand remains a partial offset to China weakness

nodes.name: Taiwan Semiconductor ADR
nodes.rationale: TSMC is sensitive to both broader semiconductor risk appetite and demand from the China supply chain.

edges.mechanism: New restrictions increase the incentive for procurement retaliation
Fabs pull forward purchases before licensing uncertainty bites
Tool uncertainty delays marginal capacity projects
Supply-chain risk creates pressure for narrow allied licenses
Domestic procurement preference reduces addressable demand
A clear exemption reduces the need for precautionary orders
Near-term pull-forward temporarily supports equipment revenue
Deferred capacity lowers equipment and materials demand
Lower China guidance reprices equipment earnings
A narrow carve-out limits the downside to global supply chains
Sector risk appetite transmits into the leading foundry valuation

summary.headline: Legacy-node controls create a short inventory pull-forward but a larger medium-term capex and vendor-guidance risk.
summary.mainUncertainty: How broadly the rule defines controlled equipment and whether allied licenses arrive quickly.
